Source: https://wwws.loc.gov/exhibits/gettysburg-address/ext/trans-hay-draft.html | Abraham Lincoln, Gettysburg Address, Hay draft, November 19, 1863, opening two paragraphs | License: public domain, U.S. federal government work (17 U.S.C. 105)
Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth, upon this continent, a new nation, conceived in Liberty, and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.

Now we are engaged in a great civil war, testing whether that nation, or any nation, so conceived, and so dedicated, can long endure. We are met here on a great battlefield of that war. We have come to dedicate a portion of it as a final resting place for those who here gave their lives that that nation might live. It is altogether fitting and proper that we should do this.
